variants.headline: Business plan abandoned before opening
variants.sub: The planned {business} will not open: {founder} has given up the plan.
variants.body:
The founder {founder} has abandoned the plan for {business} before opening. The reason given is that {why}. The builder keeps what it was paid, and any grant is owed back. For {target}, the result raises a direct question about responsibility before an enterprise can begin operating.

The company never opened. The plan has ended, but that is not the same as turning the clock back. The builder keeps the payment and any grant is owed back. Readers deserve that plain distinction before somebody makes giving up sound like a clean sheet with nothing left on it.

The responsibility of {target} should be considered through the abandoned plan and its remaining obligations. The outcome is not an operating company's failure, but the end of a proposal before opening. Readers deserve a clear story and a straight answer about responsibility.
